rounds.text: Shivalik Rasayan Ltd trades at a steep discount to its underlying assets, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.70x on a book value of ₹ 387 compared to a sector benchmark of 1.73x [E2, E7]. The company benefits from a supportive macro environment in the chemicals sector, which displays a positive tailwind score [E73, E75]. Furthermore, recent operating results demonstrate tangible momentum, including a quarterly operating margin expansion to 15% in September 2026 up from 13% a year earlier [E31], alongside net profit growth of 25% year-over-year [E65]. Balance sheet health is robust and improving, evidenced by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17x and borrowings reduced to ₹ 107 Cr in September 2026 from ₹ 123 Cr a year prior [E37, E39]. Conceded: [E13, E20, E35, E45].

Despite trading at a price-to-book ratio of 0.70x [E2], Shivalik Rasayan Ltd carries fundamental weaknesses and an unsupported valuation highlighted by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 145 per share against its market price of Rs 270, leaving a severe margin of safety of -86.6% [E45, E46]. The company generates exceptionally poor capital returns, with an ROE of 2.2% [E13], an ROCE of 4.8% [E12], and a 10-year median ROE of just 6% [E26], significantly lagging sector benchmarks across all return metrics [E8, E9, E10]. Profit generation has severely deteriorated over medium-term horizons, marked by a 5-year compounded profit growth of -7% [E19] and a 3-year compounded profit growth of -16% [E20], alongside severe cash flow contraction resulting in negative operating cash flow of Rs -34 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -51 Cr for March 2026 [E35, E36]. Institutional confidence is actively eroding through negative institutional money flow and reduced holdings from promoters, foreign institutions, and domestic institutions alike [E41, E42, E43, E44]. Conceded: [E16], [E31], [E37], [E73].

While the bear points to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 145 against a market price of Rs 270 [E45, E46], the price-to-book ratio sits deeply discounted at 0.70x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.73x [E7], and the EV/EBITDA of 9.47x is attractive against its sector benchmark of 10.42x [E11]. Although medium-term profit growth records declines over 3 and 5 years [E19, E20], the company demonstrates positive short-term momentum with 3-year compounded sales growth accelerating to 16% [E16] alongside a 25% year-on-year net profit increase [E65]. Furthermore, quarterly operating margins expanded by 2 percentage points to 15% in September 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E31], and the business operates with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17x with borrowings decreasing to Rs 107 Cr [E37, E39]. Conceded: [E13], [E12], [E35], [E36], [E41], [E42], [E43], [E44].

While the bull highlights a discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.70x and an EV/EBITDA of 9.47x [E7, E11], these low multiples reflect deeply troubled underlying returns, including an abysmal ROE of 2.2% and ROCE of 4.8% [E12, E13] that lag far behind sector benchmarks of 9.47% and 11.13% [E9, E10]. Conceded: [E7, E11]. Although the bull points to a 25% year-on-year net profit increase and a quarterly margin expansion to 15% [E31, E65], compounded profit growth over 3 and 5 years remains heavily negative at -16% and -7% [E19, E20], proving that recent quarterly ticks are anomalies rather than structural recovery. Conceded: [E31, E65]. The bull's reliance on a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17x and decreasing borrowings of Rs 107 Cr [E37, E39] completely ignores catastrophic cash generation, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -34 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -51 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. Conceded: [E37, E39]. Finally, the bull minimizes institutional withdrawal, but the evidence shows persistent negative money flow alongside declining promoter, foreign, and domestic institutional holdings [E41, E42, E43, E44].
